messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High 5xx rate detected on inference-prod-us-west /v1/generate — error_rate=48% over 5m, latency spike. Alert ID: alert-1823500000. Paging on-call: @alice. Runbook: https://wiki.redwood.ai/runbooks/inference-5xx

alice (on-call): ack — looking. pulling recent logs and checking pods and LB health.

bob (sre): I can see the spike. kube pods for model-gpu-pool-1 restarted repeatedly ~ 1823499920-1823499980. Sample tail:```
2026-05-12T14:38:12Z inference-gpu-3 ERROR upstream request failed: transport error: connection reset by peer
2026-05-12T14:38:13Z inference-gpu-3 ERROR failed to serve request: 502 from http://model-runtime:8080
```

carla (ml-eng): any OOMs in the model runtime? last deploy was a quantized variant yesterday. If the runtime is returning 502 it might be an external LB or virtualization/network issue.

dave (platform): checking infra metrics — LB 5xx rate is elevated across upstream instances in us-west-2a. Node agent logs show TLS handshake timeouts to the external model runtime host. Could be provider LB or VPC networking flakiness.

eva (vendor-liaison): I'll open an escalation with our cloud partner now (cc: @dave). Drafting the ticket with traces and pod IDs. ETA for initial response 15–20m. Ticket ref: CLOUD-32671 (created). I'm pushing for L3.

frank (support): ETA on customer-facing blurb? Ops wants a short status and an internal template for proactive emails.

alice (on-call): short status page draft: "We are experiencing elevated errors for inference requests in US-West. Engineers are investigating. Some requests may fail with 5xx. We're working to restore full service. Status: investigating — updates every 15 minutes. https://status.redwood.ai/incident/1823500000" Thoughts? :thinking_face:

gina (pm): good. Add impacted products list: Hosted API (generation), Dedicated pools in us-west. Include workaround: route traffic to us-east as a mitigation path.

bob (sre): mitigation attempts: 1) scaled up model-runtime replicas + drained suspect nodes 2) rolled traffic off 2 of 4 LB backends (manual routing) 3) temporarily disabled request batching to reduce concurrent kernel pressure. Commands used:```
# scale up replicas
kubectl -n inference scale deploy/model-runtime --replicas=12
# disable batching via configmap toggle
kubectl -n inference patch cm/inference-config -p '{"data":{"batching":"false"}}'
```

carla (ml-eng): Also rolled back to prior model patch (v2.3-quant) -> v2.1-quant to test if change introduced runtime instability. Doing a canary shift of 10% traffic to v2.1.

incident-bot: @alice acknowledged the alert. Incident timer started.

alice (on-call): vendor update? @eva

eva (vendor-liaison): Cloud provider initial reply: "Investigating high error rate on our network path to instances; seeing intermittent TLS timeouts". They've assigned an L2 engineer. Next update in 10–15m. Sharing ticket link (internal): https://cloudpartner.example/ticket/CLOUD-32671. I've attached traces and pod logs.

frank (support): here's a short customer email template to send to affected accounts (editable):

"Hello — We're currently investigating elevated 5xx errors for inference requests in our US-West region. Our engineers are working on mitigation and we're routing around impacted infrastructure. There may be intermittent failed requests; we will follow up with a resolution update within 60 minutes. If you are experiencing critical impact, please reply to this message with your account ID and a sample request id. — Redwood Inference Ops"

alice (on-call): internal comms (internal ops channel):
"Summary: Elevated 5xx on /v1/generate in US-West. Root cause suspected: provider network TLS timeouts to model-runtime; vendor escalation opened (CLOUD-32671). Mitigations: scaled replicas, disabled batching, canary rollback to v2.1-quant, partial traffic reroute to us-east. Status page posted. Next steps: monitor error rate for 15m window; if still >10% consider full failover to us-east. Handoff at 15:20 UTC to @carla. — alice"

bob (sre): monitoring update (5m after mitigations): error_rate dropped to 18% from 48%, latency P95 still elevated. Graph: https://observability.redwood.ai/d/abc/inference?from=1823499900&to=1823500300

carla (ml-eng): I've picked up the handoff early. continuing runbook steps: collecting heap profiles, checking kernel traces. If the provider says network is okay, we'll run a controlled throttling of requests to the quantized runtime to see if kernel stalls correlate.

eva (vendor-liaison): provider just pushed a fix on their edge (they rerouted some load). They reported "reduced TLS handshake timeouts after routing update". They requested we validate and keep them in the loop.

alice (on-call): validation checks:```
# smoke test to generate small token output
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-quant","input":"hello"}' | jq .
```
Responses now consistently 200 from three us-west backends. Doing a 10m continuous check.

frank (support): posted to status page: "Investigating: Elevated error rates for inference requests in US-West. Engineers are mitigating; some customers may experience failed requests. Follow for updates: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/1823500000" (update id: st-1823500000-1)

dave (platform): continuing to drain the two flaky nodes and confirmed kernel versions are up-to-date. No OOMs found.

bob (sre): 20m after mitigations error_rate=4.2%, latency P95 trending down. I'm seeing stable 200s across canary and rolled back pods.

alice (on-call): marking as "degraded" -> preparing for resolution. Drafting final customer update: "Service restored for most customers in US-West. We continue to monitor; if you still see errors, please open a ticket. Root cause: transient TLS handshake failures between provider edge and our model runtime; provider applied routing fix. Postmortem will follow." Comments?

gina (pm): add note that Dedicated customers with pinned private VPCs may need separate comms. @frank can you coordinate targeted messages to enterprise accounts?

frank (support): yes — sending targeted emails now with the final update and including steps if customers see residual errors (collect logs, request IDs).

eva (vendor-liaison): provider confirmed incident closure on their side but asked us to keep an eye for recurrence. They left the ticket open for 48h.

incident-bot: Incident status changed to: Monitoring.

alice (on-call): resolved -> final checks green over 30m. Closing the incident thread and assigning postmortem to @bob and @carla. Postmortem template: https://wiki.redwood.ai/postmortems/template. Follow-up action: create runbook tweak for provider-side TLS transient handling and add routing sanity checks to deployment pipelines.

bob (sre): grabbed action item: postmortem + RCA timeline. I'll include cloud provider timeline and the customer communications log. ETA for postmortem draft: 48h.

carla (ml-eng): I'll add model-side mitigations: finer-grained backpressure, quicker batching disable toggle, and a canary ramp playbook.

frank (support): final public status update posted: "Resolved: We have restored service for inference requests in US-West. The issue was caused by transient network TLS timeouts between provider edge and our runtime; the provider applied a routing fix. We continue monitoring. If you experience any problems, open a support ticket." (status id st-1823500000-2)

gina (pm): thanks team. nice coordination. :clap:

alice (on-call): handing off a short note to next rotation: "All green. Postmortem assigned to @bob + @carla. Keep an eye on LB TLS error rate and repeated restarts on model-runtime pods. Follow runbook link." Handoff complete.

incident-bot: Incident closed. Duration: 00:12:30.

""""
